ai.description: *Raorchestes johnceei* is a small shrub frog (SVL 22–25 mm) with a brown dorsum and distinct yellow-spotted flanks. It is identified by a prominent white vocal sac and granular skin texture.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Raorchestes johnceei* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, bright yellow or golden-yellow patch on the groin and the hidden surfaces of its thighs.
ai.habitat: *Raorchestes johnceei* inhabits high-altitude evergreen forests and shola grasslands in the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations above 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: *Raorchestes johnceei* is a nocturnal frog that primarily inhabits the canopy, where it remains active at night while foraging for small insects among the foliage.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Raorchestes johnceei* exhibits direct development, bypassing the tadpole stage. They breed during the monsoon, laying small clutches of eggs in arboreal microhabitats.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Raorchestes johnceei* is endemic to the high-altitude shola forests of the Western Ghats in Kerala, India, typically found at elevations above 2,000 meters.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Raorchestes johnceei* consists of a series of high-pitched, metallic "tink" notes, typically heard from vegetation in high-altitude forests.
